kill_chain_signals.contact: senior gets a phone call, typically on their home phone/landline, from a caller claiming to be their grandchild
kill_chain_signals.pretext: scammers claim to be someone they know, such as a grandchild, and tell them they need money immediately to avoid going to jail or to be released from jail
kill_chain_signals.payment: more than 70 money mules picking up money at victim residences in every province
kill_chain_signals.movement: CAFC successfully flagged numerous fraudulent bank accounts used to facilitate some of the occurrences

red_flags: telephone calls that require you to immediately take action and request bail money for a family member in distress
caller ID numbers that look familiar but may be spoofed
law enforcement official asking you to pay a fine or bail
email or text message claiming to be from a friend or loved one asking for money
inner voice screaming 'This doesn't sound right'
key_quote: Scammers claim to be someone they know, such as a grandchild, and tell them they need money immediately.
title: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre supports OPP in major grandparent fraud investigation
